chapters.title: Opening framework
chapters.core_thesis: Technical empire grows from the enclosure of human value and culminates in a three-reform response.

chapters.title: Social networks as infrastructure for free data capture
chapters.core_thesis: Social platforms prepared the behavioral raw material of the AI empire.

chapters.title: Social erosion and moral reconfiguration
chapters.core_thesis: Algorithmic optimization degraded attention, trust, and the moral imagination.

chapters.title: COVID as a historical accelerator
chapters.core_thesis: The health crisis consolidated digital dependency and concentrated algorithmic mediation.

chapters.title: AI arrives when the human raw material already exists
chapters.core_thesis: Foundation models emerge after a decade of free capture of human labor.

chapters.title: Talent, overhiring, valuation, and layoffs
chapters.core_thesis: AI was used as the legitimizing story for a structural financial correction.

chapters.title: AI as a dual-use rhetorical weapon
chapters.core_thesis: What is dangerous and what is cheap coexist as part of the same strategy of power.

chapters.title: Imperial control over access
chapters.core_thesis: Export controls, compute, defense alliances, and public-private chokepoints define who gets access to frontier intelligence.

chapters.title: Power network, legitimacy, and institutional capture
chapters.core_thesis: Frontier firms operate inside networks of political, media, financial, and moral legitimacy that can mature into institutional capture.

chapters.title: Future if no action is taken
chapters.core_thesis: Without intervention, AI deepens social dependency, hardens private enclosure, and stratifies access to cognition.

chapters.title: What to do
chapters.core_thesis: The response program centers three reforms: refactor Section 230, treat frontier AI weights as patrimony of humanity, and limit government capture by AI companies.
